- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.70 or 0.80 in recent days).  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or volatile (e.g., -0.30 to -0.70 in recent days).  
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; apply a 1–2 day lag correction for sudden sentiment spikes.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.  
- When sentiment is positive but price is falling, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid “sentiment-overfitting.”  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid extreme outliers (>15% above/below 14-day moving average) unless accompanied by strong event context (e.g., policy change, auction).  
- If sentiment is mixed or trending toward negative, reduce forecast slope (i.e., slow down upward momentum).
